title: Clay Pricing (2026): Actions, Data Credits and What Plans Cost
desc: Clay Launch starts at $185 a month ($167 billed yearly) and Growth at $495 ($446). How Actions and Data Credits work, rollover and the 30% top-up premium.
keywords: clay pricing, clay.com pricing, clay cost, clay launch plan, clay growth plan, clay data credits, clay actions pricing, clay enterprise pricing, clay free plan, clay credit rollover
cta: Want prospect lists built and worked for you, without the credit math?
body:
October 15, 2026. Clay charges in two currencies: Actions, which pay for the work the platform does, and Data Credits, which pay for the emails, phone numbers and company data it buys from its 150-plus data partners. The Free plan includes 500 Actions and 100 Data Credits a month. Launch starts at $185 a month, or $167 a month billed annually, with 15,000 Actions and 2,500 Data Credits a month. Growth starts at $495 a month, or $446 billed annually, with 40,000 Actions and 6,000 Data Credits, and Enterprise is priced by quote on an annual commitment. Our lead generation service builds prospect lists for outbound campaigns, so this guide breaks down what each plan includes and how the two meters add up.

Prices and rules come from Clay's pricing page and its pricing FAQ, read 15 October 2026. The plan cards show the annual-billed monthly price, while the FAQ quotes monthly billing, which is why you will see both $167 and $185 for the same plan.

Annual billing saves 10 percent, and on annual plans Clay grants all the credits up front. The Free plan has no phone number enrichment, which is the feature most outbound teams notice first.

Actions and Data Credits, explained

Clay's FAQ describes the split as two things happening at once: Clay doing work, and Clay buying data on your behalf.

  • Actions measure orchestration: enriching data, running a table, calling an AI model, sending data to another system or exporting it. Clay says Actions cost less than a cent each and get cheaper with scale, and that each plan includes enough to cover 90 percent of customers.
  • Data Credits pay for the data itself, such as an email address, a phone number or a company detail from one of Clay's partners. Clay says Data Credits get cheaper with volume.
  • Your own API keys skip Data Credits entirely. If you already pay a data provider directly, connecting its key means you only spend Actions in Clay.
  • Empty results are free: according to the FAQ, an enrichment that returns no result is not charged Data Credits or Actions. AI research columns work differently, which our breakdown of what Clay's account agents cost covers.

What extra volume costs

Both meters come in tiers, and the plan price is simply the two added together. On the Launch plan billed annually, the smallest tiers are 180,000 Actions a year for $54 a month and 30,000 Data Credits a year for $113 a month, which is the $167 headline price. Moving up the Launch plan's Data Credit tiers shows the volume discount Clay describes:

Data Credits a yearPrice a month, billed annuallyApproximate cost per credit
30,000$1134.5 cents

600,000$1,9133.8 cents

Actions fall faster: on Launch, 180,000 a year works out to about 0.36 cents each, and 2.4 million a year at $486 a month to about 0.24 cents. Growth's Data Credit tiers start higher, at 72,000 credits a year for $261 a month, and its Actions cost more: $185 a month for 480,000 a year, against $135 for the same amount on Launch.

Rollover, top-ups and the fine print

  1. Actions do not roll over. They reset each billing cycle, so unused platform capacity is lost.
  2. Data Credits do roll over, with a cap. The FAQ says unused credits on Launch and Growth can build up to twice your monthly credit amount, so a 10,000-credit plan can bank up to 20,000. The comparison table on the same page lists rollover as 15 percent of annual credits, so confirm the rule for your contract. Enterprise customers can carry over up to 15 percent of the prior year's purchased credits when they renew at an equal or higher commitment.
  3. Top-ups cost more. Buying extra credits on Launch or Growth carries a 30 percent premium over plan rates, so it is cheaper to size the tier correctly than to top up every month.

How to estimate your own Clay bill

Clay's 90 percent figure describes its customers in general, so your own data is the better guide. The practical way to budget is to build one table of 200 real prospects, run your actual waterfall, and read the credits and Actions it used. Multiply by your monthly volume, add a margin for rows that match on the second or third provider, and pick the tier that covers it without top-ups.

Remember that Clay is a data and workflow layer, not the whole outbound system. It can send email itself or through integrations, and Growth adds buying domains and email accounts for the Clay Sequencer, but deliverability still depends on how those domains and inboxes are set up and warmed up, which is what our email infrastructure setup handles. If your people search starts on LinkedIn, our guide to Sales Navigator pricing covers that side.

Clay or buying data directly

Whether Data Credits cost less than buying from a provider directly is easy to test: run a sample in Clay, note the Data Credits it used, and compare their cost at your tier with your provider's rate card. The bigger difference is the workflow. A waterfall that tries several providers in turn, signals such as job changes, and pushing results straight into your CRM or sequencer are what the Actions pay for. If you only ever use one data source and export a CSV, connecting your own API key or buying from that provider directly may cost less.

Which Clay plan to choose

  1. Testing the idea: Free, with your own API keys if you have them, and tables under 200 rows.
  2. One team running outbound: Launch, for phone numbers, job change signals and email sequencing integrations.
  3. Revenue teams that live in a CRM: Growth, for CRM auto-sync, webhooks and web intent signals.
  4. Security reviews, SSO or very high volume: Enterprise, quoted on an annual commitment.

Comparing tools? Our guides to Clay vs Apollo and Clay data enrichment cover the trade-offs. And if you would rather have the lists built, enriched and worked for you, that is what our done-for-you lead generation does.
faqs: Clay's Launch plan starts at $185 a month on monthly billing or $167 a month billed annually, and Growth starts at $495 a month or $446 billed annually. Enterprise is priced by quote on an annual commitment. There is also a Free plan with 500 Actions and 100 Data Credits a month.
What are Clay Actions and Data Credits?

Actions measure the work Clay's platform does, such as enriching rows, running tables, calling AI models and exporting data; Clay says they cost less than a cent each. Data Credits pay for data bought from Clay's 150-plus partners, such as emails, phone numbers and company details.
Does Clay have a free plan?

Yes. The Free plan includes 500 Actions and 100 Data Credits a month, unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls, Claygent and your own API keys, with tables of up to 200 rows. It does not include phone number enrichment.
Do unused Clay credits roll over?

Actions reset every billing cycle and do not roll over. Data Credits do: Clay's FAQ says unused credits on Launch and Growth can accumulate up to twice the monthly credit amount, while its comparison table lists 15 percent of annual credits, so confirm the rule for your plan. Enterprise can roll over up to 15 percent of the prior year's credits.
Does Clay charge when an enrichment finds nothing?
According to Clay's FAQ, an enrichment that returns no result is not charged Data Credits or Actions. If you bring your own API keys for a provider, you skip Data Credits and only use Actions.
Is Clay cheaper with annual billing?
Yes, by 10 percent. Launch drops from $185 to $167 a month and Growth from $495 to $446 a month when billed annually, and annual plans receive all their credits up front.
